specs.name: money_accounts
specs.description: The household's accounts in Sure with their balances, type and id.

specs.name: money_transactions
specs.description: The household's transactions in Sure, newest first, with date, name, amount, account, category and merchant; how many matched, and whether the list was cut.

account_id.description: one account, by the id money_accounts gives

category_id.description: one category, by the id money_categories gives

search.description: words in the name, notes or merchant

limit.description: how many, newest first; 25 unless given

specs.name: money_categories
specs.description: The household's transaction categories in Sure, with id and parent.

specs.name: money_net_worth
specs.description: The household's net worth in Sure: total assets, total liabilities and the difference.

specs.name: money_categorise
specs.description: Put transactions in Sure into one of the household's categories.

transaction_ids.description: the transactions, by the ids money_transactions gives; 1 to 20

category_id.description: the category, by the id money_categories gives

instructions: The money tools read the household's finances in Sure, the app they keep them in: accounts with their balances, transactions, categories and net worth. Amounts are as Sure shows them, sign and currency included. Filter transactions by the ids money_accounts and money_categories give, and say so when an answer was cut short. The one change you can make there is a transaction's category, with money_categorise, by the ids money_transactions and money_categories give, and only when the person asks for it. It never happens straight away: it is shown to the person and waits for their OK, so say that it is waiting, not that it is done.
